label: input token y during the original phase
explanation: Fires on every step where the input is the letter y during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. Dev: precision 1.0, recall 0.998. Magnitude is highest when y is the first token (t=0, at max) and falls with position: roughly 0.85x at t=2, 0.7x at t=3-4, 0.4-0.55x at t=6-7. A repeated y in the same sequence fires weaker than the first one (e.g. 1.00 then 0.92 then 0.60). It does not fire on any other token, on <DEL>, or on y fed back as input in the copy phase. The only exception is a near-zero blip (<=0.05x, 0.0% of mass) on the copy step right after an echoed y at recall_idx 1 in L=3 sequences that start with y.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.998, F1 0.999 and mass recall 0.99994. There are 0 false positives.

All 203 test misses are near-zero copy-phase blips (0.00 to 0.05x max) at step L+1 (recall_idx 1) in L=3 sequences that start with y, with y echoed as input. This matches the stated exception exactly and carries about 0.0% of the activation mass.

Checked side claims: requiring in_first==1 gives recall 0.904 on test, matching the claimed 0.90. Examples show activation falling with position (about 0.86-0.89 at t=2-3, 0.71 at t=4, 0.54-0.59 at t=5-6, 0.40 at t=7), and a repeated y fires weaker (0.71 then 0.31). Phase breakdown: 0 activations on the delimiter step and only 206 copy-phase steps in dev.
